'''The Intercontinental Derby''' ({{langx|tr|Kıtalararası Derbi}}), also known as the '''Eternal Rivalry''' (Turkish: {{Lang|tr|Ezelî Rekabet}}), is the name given to any [[basketball]] match between [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe SK]] and [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray SK]], teams of the Asian and the European parts of [[Istanbul]] respectively. Fenerbahçe is the most successful of the two clubs, having won more head to head fixtures and having clinched more trophies in the past seasons, including the highest level tier of European basketball, the [[EuroLeague]] trophy, where the winners are considered the biggest team of Europe.

==History==
According to the official records, in [[Turkey]], basketball was first played in 1904 at [[Robert College]]. An American [[physical education]] teacher laid the foundations of this sport in Turkey. Seven years later, in 1911, [[Ahmet Robenson]], a physical education teacher at a high school, decided to introduce a new game to the students. Robenson popularized this sport in Turkey.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.tbf.org.tr/tbf/tarihce/ulkemizde-basketbol | title=Türkiye Basketbol Federasyonu }}</ref><ref>Durupınar, Mehmet. ''Türk Basketbolunun 100 yıllık tarihi. (2009)''.''page(12)''.Efes Pazarlama ve Dağıtım Ticaret A.Ş. {{ISBN|978-975-00995-1-9}}</ref>

Galatasaray are considered to be the pioneers in Turkish basketball, and the sport has always been very important for the club.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/features/club-scene/i/61497/3736/the-club-scene-galatasaray-c-c | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120821090142/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/features/club-scene/i/61497/3736/the-club-scene-galatasaray-c-c | url-status=dead | archive-date=August 21, 2012 | title=Latest News &#124; Eurocup }}</ref> The team have won 11 [[Turkish Basketball Championship|national championship]] titles and 15 [[Istanbul Basketball League|Istanbul League]] titles. Former president of the club, [[Özhan Canaydın]], was a former player of the basketball team.

The men's basketball department of [[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]] was founded in 1913 and achieved considerable success when the sport established itself in Turkey. Fenerbahçe have won seven [[Istanbul Basketball League|Istanbul League]] titles and three [[Turkish Basketball Championship|national championship]] titles in 1957, 1959 and 1965, just before the [[Basketball Super League|professional nationwide league]] was founded in 1966, and participated in the [[EuroLeague|European Champions Cup]] in [[1959–60 FIBA European Champions Cup|1960]] and [[1965–66 FIBA European Champions Cup|1966]]. Their fans had to wait until 1991 for another title, when [[Levent Topsakal]], [[Larry Richard]], and head coach Çetin Yılmaz led Fenerbahçe to the Turkish League title over [[Tofaş S.K.|Tofaş]].<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/teams/showteam?clubcode=ULK Fenerbahce Ulker - Welcome to EuroLeague Basketball]</ref>

===Basketball rivalry===
[[File:Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball vs Galatasaray Men's Basketball 20170126 (8).jpg|thumb|250px|[[2016–17 EuroLeague]] match]]
Fenerbahçe consider themselves as the pioneers of basketball in Turkey, boasting their success in winning more trophies in the past seasons, including the [[2017 EuroLeague Final Four|2016–17 EuroLeague title]], which is marked as the first ever [[EuroLeague]] title won by a Turkish basketball club.

==Culture==
The clubs originate from two different sides of the [[Bosphorus]]. Fenerbahçe SK were founded in [[Kadıköy]] that is located on the Asian side of Istanbul, while Galatasaray SK were founded in the [[Beyoğlu|Beyoğlu district]], on the European side of Istanbul. Both clubs naturally draw the majority of their support from the side of the city that they are native to, but maintain a significant majority of support drawn from the rest of Turkey.
